flow._: The one definition of the n8n flow: each phase, the node operation that does it, the example workflow and node that run it, and what it costs. The README (flow.mjs --write), the tests (flow.test.mjs), the CLI demo (taifoon demo n8n) and the page www.taifoon.io/docs/n8n all read this file. Edit it here, then run node examples/flow.mjs --write.

network.label: Taifoon devnet 36927: test tokens (dUSDC) with no value

roles.title: Buyer
roles.line: Say what you need in words. The layer matches a seller, hires it, grades the reply by code and settles; you verify it against the chain.

phases.title: Key
phases.does: Get a free key for a wallet label (nothing is signed) and read its tenant.
phases.costs: free: 3 keys a day per IP

phases.title: Tenant
phases.does: Who the saved key belongs to, its keys and the next step.

phases.title: Demand
phases.does: Post the need in words. A dry run first shows the class, the input read from the words and the cover preview, and keeps nothing.
phases.costs: free on the devnet: the key's own demand budget

phases.title: Match
phases.does: The auto-match loop (every 2 minutes) claims the demand and ranks the class's sellers by their own record: open → claimed → matched.

phases.title: Handshake
phases.does: The broker offers the job to the chosen seller in its own protocol and holds the reply: the seller, the ranking and the reply digest.

phases.title: Job
phases.does: The job is funded on the devnet, the reply is graded by the class's own check (no model), and the job settles: hired → graded → settling → settled.
phases.costs: free: code grades spend no credit; the devnet escrow uses test tokens

phases.title: Attest
phases.does: Re-derive the settle transaction and the payee from chain before anyone acts on the result: REAL, FABRICATED or UNVERIFIED.

phases.title: Explorer
phases.does: The job as the explorer shows it: who did the work, who the chain paid, the grade and every transaction with its link.

roles.title: Seller
roles.line: List an n8n workflow as a seller, take jobs on its hire webhook, and hand finished work to the relayer.

phases.title: Claim
phases.does: Claim the seller workflow by its card URL. The answer carries a nonce for the card field taifoon_listing.
phases.costs: free (any key, a free key included)

phases.title: Verify
phases.does: The layer reads the card for the nonce and sends one class probe to the hire webhook, graded by the class's check. A pass lists the workflow.

phases.title: Jobs
phases.does: Jobs arrive on the hire webhook when the loop hires the listing; the job feed shows the jobs an address sells, with a cursor.

phases.title: Completion
phases.does: Hand a finished job to the relayer with its proof transaction. Idempotent on job ID + nonce: a repeat returns the first outcome and never a second transaction.

phases.title: Status
phases.does: Poll the completion until it is recorded or settled.

roles.title: Around the flow
roles.line: Public reads that need no key: who can do what, what the guarantee costs, and whether a transaction is inside the root.

phases.title: Discover
phases.does: What n8n templates and nodes can do, the skill vocabulary, the standards deployed, agent cards and the market; then one provider's record.

phases.title: Assure
phases.does: Price the guarantee from one seller's settled record and build the unsigned fund-job calls. Nothing is signed or sent.
phases.costs: free: a plan, never a transaction

phases.title: Prove
phases.does: The latest superroot, then the inclusion proof of one transaction with exactly what was checked.

grid.earn: GRID points are earned by bringing a resource the oracle can probe (an RPC endpoint, storage, a GPU) and settle as soulbound GRID every 6 h. Running these workflows earns no GRID.
grid.spend: Settled GRID pays for Jev grades and gateway credit at the USDC price (1 GRID = 0.01 USDC), signed by the wallet that holds it.
grid.in_this_flow: Nothing in these examples spends credit: demands settle on the devnet, the grades are code grades, and every read is free. A Jev grade (Judge resource) is the first step that spends: 3 free on a key, then a block of 3 for 0.15 USDC or 15 GRID.

1a-free-key-and-tenant.json.name: Taifoon example 1a: get a free key and check its tenant
1a-free-key-and-tenant.json.description: Registers a free Taifoon key for a wallet label (no credential needed), reads the new tenant with that key, and returns the tenant and key prefixes only. The keys appear once, in the Register Free Key output; successful runs are not saved.

output.save_it: Copy api_key from the Register Free Key output into Credentials → Taifoon Relayer API now. It is not shown again.

1b-my-tenant.json.name: Taifoon example 1b: check my tenant (with the saved key)
1b-my-tenant.json.description: Reads the tenant of the key saved in the Taifoon Relayer API credential: who it is, its keys, its next step and its own traffic.

2-buyer-need-to-verified.json.name: Taifoon example 2: buyer (a need in words → matched → hired → graded → settled → verified)
2-buyer-need-to-verified.json.description: Posts a need in words. The layer maps it to a job class by fixed rules (preview first, kept nothing), matches a seller, opens the handshake, grades the reply by code and settles on the Taifoon devnet 36927 (test tokens, no value). The workflow polls the demand, reads the handshake and the explorer row, and re-derives the settle transaction from chain with Verify Hire Claim before it hands back the result.

preview.how: mcp.digest: 2 of its intent rules matched the words (the next class: 0), and its input was read from them

3-seller-claim-verify-complete.json.name: Taifoon example 3: seller (claim a listing → verify → receive jobs → submit completion)
3-seller-claim-verify-complete.json.description: Lists an n8n seller workflow with the layer (claim its card, the card serves the nonce, verify: the layer reads the card and runs one class probe), then polls for jobs where the seller address is the provider and hands a finished job to the relayer (idempotent on job ID + nonce) and reads its status.

last_probe.why: mcp.digest: every decisive check passed (nonce_echo, task_bound, no_tool_error, digest_exact)

4-discovery-to-reputation.json.name: Taifoon example 4: discovery (capabilities, skills, standards, cards, market → pick a provider → reputation)
4-discovery-to-reputation.json.description: Reads what is out there with public reads only (no credential): what n8n templates and nodes can do, the skill vocabulary, which standards are deployed where, agent cards with an owner and a published skill, the market statistics. Picks a provider from the cards and checks its reputation in the public job log.

reputation.note: Counts from the public job log, not a score. Verify a specific job through /v1/proof/tx before relying on it.

5-assurance-quote-and-plan.json.name: Taifoon example 5: assurance (pools → quote → unsigned fund-job calls; plan only)
5-assurance-quote-and-plan.json.description: Reads the coverage pools, picks the seller with the longest settled record, prices the guarantee for one job from that record, and builds the unsigned fund-job calls on the Taifoon devnet 36927. Nothing is signed or sent: the output is the calldata, its effect in words and who must sign it.

record.source: every ERC-8183 job this seller took (2887): 2735 completed and paid, 5 delivered then rejected or paid and never delivered; rejected-before-delivery, unpaid and open jobs excluded

premium.basis: the upper bound of the 95% Wilson interval on this seller’s cheat rate, applied to the price

calls.effect: Lets the assurance hook move up to 10042 of this token from your address for this job. Nothing moves until the job is funded.

Locks 10042 in escrow from you and 20000 from the seller, creating the insured job. The seller must have approved the hook for exactly this deposit first — for this job, after agreeing to it. A seller should never leave a standing allowance to the hook: the live contract pulls the deposit from whichever seller the funder names.
calls.signer: the buyer, after the seller has approved its deposit

output.note: Send these in order from the named signer. Nothing was signed here and no key is held.
output.signed_or_sent: nothing: hand these to the named signer, in order

6-proof-root-and-tx.json.name: Taifoon example 6: proof (latest root → transaction proof → output)
6-proof-root-and-tx.json.description: Reads the latest superroot and how long ago it was anchored, then asks for the inclusion proof of one Base transaction, waiting while the producer is still building that block's proof, and returns exactly what was checked.

output.source: receipt read from chain; block proof from the producer; block hash compared between the two
output.verdict: proof served: the transaction is inside the root
